cards.name: Identity & Access Policy
cards.flavour: Who may be who, and how we prove it
cards.desc: Board-endorsed policy that sets identity assurance levels, MFA expectations and account lifecycle rules. Without it, authentication controls are optional in practice.
cards.lesson: Board-endorsed policy that sets identity assurance levels, MFA expectations and account lifecycle rules. Without it, authentication controls are optional in practice.

cards.name: Change Management Board
cards.flavour: Nothing ships without a name on it
cards.desc: Formal change control: approvals, separation between requester and deployer, and rollback plans. Unauthorised change is Tampering by another name.
cards.lesson: Formal change control: approvals, separation between requester and deployer, and rollback plans. Unauthorised change is Tampering by another name.

cards.name: Logging & Retention Standard
cards.flavour: If it is not logged it did not happen
cards.desc: Defines what must be logged, for how long, and who may delete it. Sets the evidentiary baseline for every investigation and regulator question.
cards.lesson: Defines what must be logged, for how long, and who may delete it. Sets the evidentiary baseline for every investigation and regulator question.

cards.name: Data Classification Policy
cards.flavour: Label it before you lose it
cards.desc: A classification scheme with handling rules per tier. Drives encryption, access and DLP decisions and decides what a breach actually costs.
cards.lesson: A classification scheme with handling rules per tier. Drives encryption, access and DLP decisions and decides what a breach actually costs.

cards.name: Resilience & Impact Tolerance
cards.flavour: How long can we be down? Write it down
cards.desc: Board-set maximum tolerable downtime for critical services, funded and tested. Turns “availability” from a wish into a requirement.
cards.lesson: Board-set maximum tolerable downtime for critical services, funded and tested. Turns “availability” from a wish into a requirement.

cards.name: Separation of Duties
cards.flavour: No one person holds every key
cards.desc: Policy that splits request, approve and execute for sensitive actions. Limits what a single stolen or malicious privileged account can do.
cards.lesson: Policy that splits request, approve and execute for sensitive actions. Limits what a single stolen or malicious privileged account can do.

cards.name: Identity Inventory
cards.flavour: Humans, services, keys, bots — all of them
cards.desc: A complete inventory of human, service and machine identities and their owners. Orphaned service accounts are a favourite foothold.
cards.lesson: A complete inventory of human, service and machine identities and their owners. Orphaned service accounts are a favourite foothold.

cards.name: Software Bill of Materials
cards.flavour: Know what is inside the box
cards.desc: SBOMs and provenance records for software and firmware so a poisoned component can be found and scoped in hours.
cards.lesson: SBOMs and provenance records for software and firmware so a poisoned component can be found and scoped in hours.

cards.name: Log Source Inventory
cards.flavour: Map every blind spot
cards.desc: An inventory of what generates telemetry, what is collected and what is silent. Gaps here become “we cannot tell what happened”.
cards.lesson: An inventory of what generates telemetry, what is collected and what is silent. Gaps here become “we cannot tell what happened”.

cards.name: Data Flow Mapping
cards.flavour: Where does the sensitive stuff actually go?
cards.desc: Diagrams and discovery tooling showing where sensitive data is stored, processed and transmitted. The raw material of every threat model.
cards.lesson: Diagrams and discovery tooling showing where sensitive data is stored, processed and transmitted. The raw material of every threat model.

cards.name: Critical Dependency Map
cards.flavour: The thing the thing depends on
cards.desc: Maps the services, suppliers and utilities each critical function needs — including the boring ones like DNS, power and the one SaaS nobody remembers.
cards.lesson: Maps the services, suppliers and utilities each critical function needs — including the boring ones like DNS, power and the one SaaS nobody remembers.

cards.name: Attack Path Mapping
cards.flavour: See the route to Domain Admin first
cards.desc: Graph-based analysis of privilege relationships and attack paths, plus authenticated vulnerability scanning, so the shortest path to crown jewels is closed before an attacker walks it.
cards.lesson: Graph-based analysis of privilege relationships and attack paths, plus authenticated vulnerability scanning, so the shortest path to crown jewels is closed before an attacker walks it.

cards.name: Phishing-Resistant MFA
cards.flavour: FIDO2 beats a lookalike login page
cards.desc: Hardware-bound, origin-checked authenticators (FIDO2/passkeys) that cannot be replayed by an adversary-in-the-middle. The single highest-value identity control.
cards.lesson: Hardware-bound, origin-checked authenticators (FIDO2/passkeys) that cannot be replayed by an adversary-in-the-middle. The single highest-value identity control.

cards.name: Code Signing & Integrity Checks
cards.flavour: Trust the signature, not the filename
cards.desc: Cryptographic signing of code, firmware and configuration, verified at install and boot. Stops unauthorised modification being silently accepted.
cards.lesson: Cryptographic signing of code, firmware and configuration, verified at install and boot. Stops unauthorised modification being silently accepted.

cards.name: Tamper-Evident Audit Logging
cards.flavour: Logs the intruder cannot quietly edit
cards.desc: Logs shipped off-host to append-only storage with integrity protection, so an intruder with local admin cannot erase their trail.
cards.lesson: Logs shipped off-host to append-only storage with integrity protection, so an intruder with local admin cannot erase their trail.

cards.name: Encryption In Transit & At Rest
cards.flavour: Make a stolen disk a boring disk
cards.desc: TLS everywhere and strong at-rest encryption with managed keys. Turns many data-theft events into non-events.
cards.lesson: TLS everywhere and strong at-rest encryption with managed keys. Turns many data-theft events into non-events.

cards.name: Rate Limiting & DDoS Shield
cards.flavour: Absorb the flood, serve the humans
cards.desc: Upstream scrubbing, rate limits, autoscaling and sane timeouts so volumetric and application-layer floods degrade gracefully.
cards.lesson: Upstream scrubbing, rate limits, autoscaling and sane timeouts so volumetric and application-layer floods degrade gracefully.

cards.name: Least Privilege & PAM
cards.flavour: Admin rights are a loan, not a gift
cards.desc: Role-based access with just-in-time elevation, vaulted privileged credentials and no standing admin. Limits blast radius when any one account falls.
cards.lesson: Role-based access with just-in-time elevation, vaulted privileged credentials and no standing admin. Limits blast radius when any one account falls.

cards.name: Identity Threat Detection
cards.flavour: Impossible travel, impossible Tuesday
cards.desc: Behavioural analytics on sign-ins and sessions: impossible travel, token replay, MFA fatigue patterns and anomalous consent grants.
cards.lesson: Behavioural analytics on sign-ins and sessions: impossible travel, token replay, MFA fatigue patterns and anomalous consent grants.

cards.name: File Integrity Monitoring
cards.flavour: Tell me when the binary changes
cards.desc: Baseline hashes and alerts on unexpected changes to critical files, configs and firmware. Catches implants and web shells.
cards.lesson: Baseline hashes and alerts on unexpected changes to critical files, configs and firmware. Catches implants and web shells.

cards.name: SIEM Correlation
cards.flavour: One alert is noise, five is a story
cards.desc: Correlates events across sources to turn scattered log lines into a timeline. The heart of a SOC.
cards.lesson: Correlates events across sources to turn scattered log lines into a timeline. The heart of a SOC.

cards.name: DLP & Egress Anomaly Detection
cards.flavour: Why is the file server talking to Moldova?
cards.desc: Content-aware and volumetric detection of data leaving the environment, including slow-drip exfiltration over allowed channels.
cards.lesson: Content-aware and volumetric detection of data leaving the environment, including slow-drip exfiltration over allowed channels.

cards.name: Saturation & Health Monitoring
cards.flavour: The graph went vertical at 03:12
cards.desc: Capacity, latency and error-budget monitoring that spots degradation before customers do and separates attack from success.
cards.lesson: Capacity, latency and error-budget monitoring that spots degradation before customers do and separates attack from success.

cards.name: Privilege Escalation Analytics
cards.flavour: Why did svc-backup become Domain Admin?
cards.desc: Alerts on privilege grants, group changes, token manipulation and use of privileged functions outside change windows.
cards.lesson: Alerts on privilege grants, group changes, token manipulation and use of privileged functions outside change windows.

cards.name: Credential Revocation & Session Kill
cards.flavour: Reset it all. Now.
cards.desc: Rapid, rehearsed ability to revoke sessions, tokens, API keys and passwords for suspected-compromised identities across every system.
cards.lesson: Rapid, rehearsed ability to revoke sessions, tokens, API keys and passwords for suspected-compromised identities across every system.

cards.name: Host Isolation & Quarantine
cards.flavour: Pull the cable, keep the evidence
cards.desc: EDR-driven network containment of compromised hosts that preserves memory and disk state for analysis.
cards.lesson: EDR-driven network containment of compromised hosts that preserves memory and disk state for analysis.

cards.name: Forensic Evidence Preservation
cards.flavour: Chain of custody or it never happened
cards.desc: Collect and protect volatile and persistent evidence with integrity guarantees so findings stand up to regulators, insurers and courts.
cards.lesson: Collect and protect volatile and persistent evidence with integrity guarantees so findings stand up to regulators, insurers and courts.

cards.name: Breach Notification Playbook
cards.flavour: The 72-hour clock is already running
cards.desc: Pre-agreed decision tree, drafts and contacts for regulator, customer and partner notification. Legal duties start at awareness, not at root cause.
cards.lesson: Pre-agreed decision tree, drafts and contacts for regulator, customer and partner notification. Legal duties start at awareness, not at root cause.

cards.name: Traffic Scrubbing & Failover
cards.flavour: Shift the load before the pager melts
cards.desc: Runbooks to activate scrubbing, traffic diversion and failover regions during a sustained attack.
cards.lesson: Runbooks to activate scrubbing, traffic diversion and failover regions during a sustained attack.

cards.name: Emergency Privilege Revocation
cards.flavour: Break glass, then break their access
cards.desc: Break-glass procedures to strip standing and delegated privilege, rotate privileged secrets and lock down admin tiers mid-incident.
cards.lesson: Break-glass procedures to strip standing and delegated privilege, rotate privileged secrets and lock down admin tiers mid-incident.

cards.name: Identity Rebuild & Re-proofing
cards.flavour: Trust no one until re-verified
cards.desc: Re-issue credentials and re-verify identities after compromise, including help-desk procedures resistant to social engineering.
cards.lesson: Re-issue credentials and re-verify identities after compromise, including help-desk procedures resistant to social engineering.

cards.name: Golden Image Rebuild
cards.flavour: Rebuild, do not clean
cards.desc: Rebuild compromised systems from known-good, signed images and verified config rather than trusting a “cleaned” host.
cards.lesson: Rebuild compromised systems from known-good, signed images and verified config rather than trusting a “cleaned” host.

cards.name: Post-Incident Review
cards.flavour: Blameless, evidence-led, actually actioned
cards.desc: Structured lessons-learned that feed back into detections, playbooks and risk register. Closes the loop to Govern.
cards.lesson: Structured lessons-learned that feed back into detections, playbooks and risk register. Closes the loop to Govern.

cards.name: Secret & Key Rotation
cards.flavour: Assume every key in memory is burned
cards.desc: Fast, automated rotation of keys, certificates and secrets that may have been exposed, with revocation of the old material.
cards.lesson: Fast, automated rotation of keys, certificates and secrets that may have been exposed, with revocation of the old material.

cards.name: Immutable Backups & Tested Restore
cards.flavour: A backup you have not restored is a hope
cards.desc: Offline or immutable backups with regular restoration tests against defined recovery objectives. Your answer to ransomware.
cards.lesson: Offline or immutable backups with regular restoration tests against defined recovery objectives. Your answer to ransomware.

cards.name: Directory & Trust Rebuild
cards.flavour: Reset krbtgt. Twice.
cards.desc: Procedures to recover the identity plane itself — forest recovery, trust re-establishment, tiered rebuild — when the attacker owned the directory.
cards.lesson: Procedures to recover the identity plane itself — forest recovery, trust re-establishment, tiered rebuild — when the attacker owned the directory.

cards.name: Emergency Patch
cards.desc: Patch the exploited component now. ACSC expects exploited vulnerabilities in internet-facing services to be patched within 48 hours.
cards.lesson: Patch internet-facing services fast when exploitation is known: Essential Eight “patch applications”.

cards.name: Network Segmentation
cards.desc: Zone the asset. Adversary Spread into or out of it costs 1 more energy and has 1 less power.
cards.lesson: Segmentation turns one foothold into a contained incident; IEC 62443 calls the boundaries zones and conduits.

cards.name: EDR with Auto-Containment
cards.desc: Detects on this asset and, each round, reduces the grip of revealed footholds here by 1.
cards.lesson: Endpoint detection and response combines telemetry with containment actions; speed matters more than perfect fidelity.

cards.name: WAF & Virtual Patching
cards.desc: Blocks known exploit patterns in front of an internet-facing app while the real fix is prepared.
cards.lesson: A WAF buys time for patching; it is not a substitute for fixing the flaw.

cards.name: Awareness Training & Phishing Simulation
cards.desc: People are a control layer too. Counts against social-engineering techniques that ATT&CK lists User Training for.
cards.lesson: User training reduces — never eliminates — social engineering success; pair it with technical controls.

cards.name: Threat Hunt
cards.desc: Hypothesis-driven hunting: reveal up to 2 hidden footholds anywhere, whatever their stealth (up to 5).
cards.lesson: Hunting finds what detection rules miss; it starts from an adversary hypothesis, ideally a specific ATT&CK technique.

cards.name: Tabletop Exercise
cards.desc: See the adversary’s next moves clearly and draw a card.
cards.lesson: Exercising the scenario before it happens is the cheapest control in the programme.

cards.name: Purple Team Exercise
cards.desc: Reveal a foothold, expose the adversary’s tradecraft (+2 Exposure), draw a card.
cards.lesson: Red and blue working together turns each emulated technique into a detection or control improvement.

cards.name: SOAR Automation
cards.desc: The first time each round a foothold is revealed, its grip is reduced by 1 automatically.
cards.lesson: Automate the first response step — containment in seconds — and keep humans for judgement.

cards.name: Zero Trust Architecture
cards.desc: Assets with 2 or more controls gain +1 ward against every property.
cards.lesson: Zero trust is layered verification of identity, device and context for every request, not a single product.

cards.name: Essential Eight Maturity Uplift
cards.desc: Every Protect control gains +1 ward on its own property.
cards.lesson: The Essential Eight maturity model measures how consistently controls are implemented, not just whether they exist.

cards.name: Assume Breach
cards.desc: At the start of each of your turns, reveal the hidden foothold with the lowest stealth.
cards.lesson: Design and operate as if the adversary is already inside — then compromise is a routine to detect, not a surprise.

cards.name: Cyber Insurance
cards.desc: The first Resilience loss each round is reduced by 2.
cards.lesson: Insurance transfers financial loss; underwriters increasingly require MFA, EDR and tested backups.

cards.name: Technical Debt
cards.desc: Unplayable. Clogs your hand until you pay it down (Decommission it at a Rest site or shop).
cards.lesson: Deferred maintenance and unmanaged exceptions accrue interest in the form of risk.

cards.name: Number Matching
cards.desc: Push approvals now need the number shown at login. Counters MFA-fatigue (push bombing).
cards.lesson: Plain push MFA is defeated by Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation (T1621). Number matching forces the user to prove presence at the login screen.

cards.name: FIDO2 / Passkeys
cards.desc: +2 Authentication ward. Origin-bound credentials: counters MFA fatigue and adversary-in-the-middle phishing.
cards.lesson: Phishing-resistant authenticators bind the credential to the legitimate origin, so a lookalike site or a relayed session gets nothing usable. (ATT&CK lists no mitigation for T1557 under MFA; the adversary-in-the-middle resistance here comes from NIST SP 800-63B guidance.)

cards.name: Conditional Access
cards.desc: +1 Authentication and Authorisation ward: sign-ins need a compliant device and acceptable risk.
cards.lesson: Context-aware policy (device health, location, risk) makes stolen credentials alone insufficient.

cards.name: Credential Guard
cards.desc: Isolates secrets from the OS. Counters OS credential dumping and Kerberos ticket theft.
cards.lesson: LSASS dumping (T1003.001) is a staple of ransomware and nation-state intrusions; virtualisation-based credential isolation removes the easy target.

cards.name: Just-in-Time Privilege
cards.desc: +1 Authorisation ward. Privileged footholds on this asset lose their privilege at the start of each round.
cards.lesson: Standing admin rights are a loan the attacker can call in. Time-boxed elevation shrinks the window.

cards.name: Tiered Admin Model
cards.desc: +2 Authorisation ward: domain-admin credentials never touch lower tiers.
cards.lesson: Credential tiering stops one compromised workstation from handing over the directory.

cards.name: TLS 1.3 + HSTS
cards.desc: +1 Confidentiality ward. Counters network sniffing and adversary-in-the-middle on this asset.
cards.lesson: Strong transport encryption with pinned expectations removes passive sniffing and most downgrade tricks.

cards.name: Customer-Managed Keys (KMS/HSM)
cards.desc: +1 Confidentiality ward. Keys live in a hardened module with separate access control.
cards.lesson: Separating key custody from data custody means a data breach is not automatically a key breach.

cards.name: Post-Quantum Hybrid Crypto
cards.desc: +2 Confidentiality ward. Immunises this asset against “harvest now, decrypt later”.
cards.lesson: Adversaries can steal encrypted data today and decrypt it once quantum computers mature. NIST has standardised ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and signature schemes (FIPS 204/205) and is planning the retirement of quantum-vulnerable algorithms (NIST IR 8547).

cards.name: Application Allowlisting
cards.desc: +2 Integrity ward. Only approved code runs: counters user execution, scripting and LOLBin proxy execution.
cards.lesson: The Essential Eight’s most effective strategy against commodity malware; also blunts living-off-the-land tradecraft when rules cover script hosts and proxy binaries.

cards.name: SBOM + Build Provenance
cards.desc: +1 Integrity ward. Counters supply-chain compromise by verifying what you build and deploy.
cards.lesson: You cannot patch or contain a poisoned component you cannot find: inventories and signed provenance make that a query.

cards.name: Secure Boot & Firmware Signing
cards.desc: Counters pre-OS boot implants and firmware corruption.
cards.lesson: Boot integrity extends trust from silicon up; bootkits and firmware implants survive reinstalls.

cards.name: Anycast CDN & DDoS Scrubbing
cards.desc: +2 Availability ward. Counters volumetric network denial of service.
cards.lesson: Absorb floods upstream where capacity is cheap; protect the origin by only accepting traffic from the edge.

cards.name: Autoscaling & Graceful Degradation
cards.desc: +1 Availability ward. The asset recovers 1 integrity at the start of each round.
cards.lesson: Designing for partial failure keeps core functions up while capacity returns.

cards.name: WORM Log Storage
cards.desc: +1 Non-repudiation ward. Counters indicator removal and event-log clearing.
cards.lesson: Write-once, off-host logging makes evidence deletion an alert instead of a cover-up.

cards.name: EDR Telemetry
cards.desc: +1 detection strength on this monitor.
cards.lesson: Richer telemetry raises the signal-to-noise ratio of every analytic that sits on top.

cards.name: Detection-as-Code (Sigma)
cards.desc: +1 detection strength. Footholds created through execution techniques here get 1 less stealth.
cards.lesson: Treat detections like software: version them, test them against ATT&CK-mapped emulations, and share them as Sigma rules.

cards.name: Hypothesis-Driven Hunting
cards.desc: This monitor reveals 1 additional foothold each round.
cards.lesson: Human-led hunting finds the activity your rules were never written for.

cards.name: UEBA Baselines
cards.desc: +1 detection strength, +1 more against privileged footholds.
cards.lesson: Behavioural baselines catch valid-account abuse that signature matching cannot.

cards.name: Canary Tokens & Honeytokens
cards.desc: The first Credential Access or Collection card the adversary plays here reveals its foothold and gives +2 Exposure.
cards.lesson: Decoy credentials and files produce near-zero-false-positive alerts the moment an intruder touches them.

cards.name: Immutable Backups
cards.desc: Your recovery control revives an asset for 2 more integrity.
cards.lesson: Backups that cannot be altered or deleted by the production environment survive the ransomware that hits it.

cards.name: Air-Gapped Vault
cards.desc: Counters ransomware, wipers and recovery inhibition; adjacent Strike spillover cannot reach it.
cards.lesson: Offline copies sit outside the blast radius; ransomware crews delete reachable backups first (T1490).
